sections.h2: Where is Cabot, Arkansas, and what is its history?
sections.html:
Cabot is the largest city in Lonoke County, in the northwest part of the county, and it belongs to the Little Rock-North Little Rock-Conway metro area. It began in 1873 as a refueling stop on the Cairo and Fulton Railroad after the line bypassed nearby Austin, and it was incorporated on November 9, 1891.

Growth came in waves. The 1955 opening of Little Rock Air Force Base in Jacksonville brought families, and federal desegregation orders for the Little Rock School District in 1972 sent more to surrounding towns. Cabot's census population rose from 1,321 in 1960 to 8,319 in 1990, 15,261 in 2000, 23,776 in 2010 and 26,569 in 2020. The 2025 estimate is 27,711.

One event still shapes the downtown layout. A tornado struck Cabot on March 29, 1976, killing five people and destroying several buildings, and City Plaza was built on the rebuilt site. City Hall, the municipal courtroom and the police station now sit there.

sections.h2: How does the highway and Air Force Base connection affect Cabot housing?
sections.html:
Cabot sits along Interstate 57 and U.S. 67 and 167, a four-lane freeway on the northwest side of the city that leads about 22 miles southwest to Little Rock. Searcy is 26 miles northeast, and Jacksonville is 9 miles southwest on the same route.

That route links Cabot to two big sources of buyers. Many residents commute to Little Rock, and the city is described as a commuter town. Little Rock Air Force Base in Jacksonville is the other draw: about 40 percent of its military personnel are reported to live in Cabot, and the school district holds a Purple Star designation for supporting military families.

What this means if you sell in Cabot:

  • A seller with orders or a job transfer may care more about a firm closing date than a long listing period.
  • Distance to the freeway and to Jacksonville or Little Rock is a fact worth stating up front.
  • Buyers who commute will ask how far the house is from the on-ramp.

sections.h2: What is the climate in Cabot, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
Cabot has a humid subtropical climate with hot, humid summers and mild to cool winters. The July mean high is 92.4 degrees and the January mean high is 51.2 degrees, with a record high of 112 degrees and a record low of minus 7. The city gets about 53 inches of precipitation over roughly 92 days a year, and about 2 inches of snow.

The 1976 tornado is a reminder that severe weather is part of life here. Buyers and appraisers commonly ask about:

  • Roof age, shingle condition and prior storm claims.
  • Windows, doors and garage doors that have taken wind damage.
  • Moisture in attics, crawl spaces and slabs after wet seasons.
  • Cooling system age.

Damage you have not repaired does not have to hold up a sale. A buyer who purchases as-is will price the work instead of asking you to finish it.

Cabot Public Schools serve Cabot, Austin and Ward, plus most of northern Lonoke County. The district includes Cabot High School and Cabot Junior High School North, which was rebuilt after a fire on August 10, 2006 destroyed the old building. No one was hurt in that fire.

Because the district reaches beyond city limits, a mailing address that says Cabot does not always mean the same district boundary. Check the school assignment for the specific parcel before you list or discuss it with a buyer.

sections.h2: What permits and city offices matter when you sell in Cabot?
sections.html:
Cabot's Planning and Zoning department at 1 City Plaza, Suite A handles residential permits and the zoning map. The city lists permits for additions and remodels, decks, electrical, plumbing and mechanical work, swimming pools, water heater replacement, generators, roofs, solar panels, sprinkler systems, storage buildings, sun rooms, porch enclosures and retaining walls.

The city's page says homeowners may do many repairs themselves but still need permits and must follow code, and it says that contractors should have purchased the permit for the work. The page says the work requires one or more inspections depending on the job.

Planning and Zoning can be reached at 501-843-4819. The city's GIS map has a zoning layer and the city recommends checking it before applying for a planning permit.

Before listing, look back at any work done on the house: a new roof, a deck, a water heater or an accessory building. If a permit was never pulled, ask the department what to do. A cash buyer will usually take a house that way, though you should tell them what you know.

sections.h2: How are property taxes handled for a house sale in Cabot?
sections.html:
Arkansas real property tax is due between the first business day of March and October 15 of the year after the levy, and the collector adds a 10 percent penalty to balances left after October 15. State law lets taxpayers pay in installments: one quarter by the third Monday in April, one quarter by the third Monday in July, and the final half by October 15.

Cabot properties are billed through the Lonoke County collector along with the rest of the county, and the state's property tax portal lists a Lonoke County payment page. Because tax is paid in arrears, the person who owns the house on the assessment date is billed for the year, and the closing statement decides how the amount is split between buyer and seller.

Arkansas also charges a real property transfer tax of $3.30 per $1,000 of the consideration on transfers above $100. Read the state transfer tax page for the official wording.

sections.h2: Camp Nelson, events and the wider county around Cabot
sections.html:
Cabot sits next to places with long histories. In 1862 a typhoid epidemic killed about 1,500 Confederate soldiers camped in the hills around Cabot and Austin, and in 1905 veterans moved 428 graves to the Camp Nelson Confederate Cemetery. Volunteers from Cabot began maintaining it in 1982.

The city also holds Cabotfest each October downtown and Strawberry Fest each spring, a nod to the strawberries once shipped from the area by rail. The city has 43 churches and two country clubs, Greystone on the north end and Rolling Hills in the southeast.

The county beyond town is rural. Lonoke County moved from cotton to rice after a 1904 demonstration, rice farming remains part of its economy, and waterways such as Bayou Meto and the Big Ditch run through it. Acreage and country houses outside the city limits can raise different questions than a subdivision lot inside Cabot, so tell a buyer exactly where your parcel lies.

sections.h2: What do Cabot sellers usually face?
sections.html:
Sellers here often have a house that needs updating, a job transfer, a rental with tenants, or an inherited house with several owners. The Air Force Base link means some owners have only weeks to move.

Compare a listing with a cash sale on timing, repair costs and what you keep in the end. Local rules differ from town to town, and Cabot has its own zoning code, so confirm anything that affects your house with city staff.

faqs.q: What county is Cabot, Arkansas in?
faqs.a: Cabot is in Lonoke County, and it is the county's largest city. The county seat is the city of Lonoke.

faqs.q: How far is Cabot from Little Rock?
faqs.a: About 22 miles southwest on the I-57 and U.S. 67 and 167 freeway. Jacksonville is 9 miles from Cabot on the same route.

faqs.q: When are Arkansas property taxes due for a Cabot house?
faqs.a: They are due by October 15, with a 10 percent penalty on unpaid balances after that date. Collection starts the first business day of March, and installments are allowed under state law.

faqs.q: Do I need permits for repairs on my Cabot house?
faqs.a: Yes for many jobs. Cabot lists permits for roofs, water heaters, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, decks, pools, generators and similar work. Call Planning and Zoning at 501-843-4819 if you are not sure.
Cabot Public Schools serves Cabot, Austin and Ward and most of northern Lonoke County. Confirm the district for your exact address.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Cabot house as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. You can sell as-is to a cash buyer, who will account for repairs in the price. Tell the buyer about any known problems.
